about.title: Scenario list of the final run of the HALAH prototype
about.pass_rule: A scenario passes when the observed decision or outcome equals the expected one, the observed deny code equals the expected one (null means that no deny code is shown and none is written), and the failed checks are the expected ones. Observed values are read from the ledger rows in the database file of the run, from the receipts and from the answers of the calls, never from the text of a page.
about.deny_code_rule: A deny code is one of the nine or null. A failure of V_I, of V_A, of the proof or of the sealed copy is named as a failed check and has no code. The reason of a refused revocation, of a refused approval and of the verifier contract is an outcome, not a deny code.

runs_in.browser: the running application, driven in a browser by tools/final_run.py
runs_in.service call: a function of the services of the same build, called in the process of the tool on copies of the records, with a ledger of its own. It writes to no store of the running application
runs_in.contract call: a read or a call (eth_call) against the deployed contracts. Nothing is sent and no gas is spent
runs_in.test suite: the automated tests named in the entry, taken from the test-suite output of the same run

stages.1: the day of the run, before midnight of the server clock: Chapters 5, 6 and 7 and the case study up to the registrar
stages.2: after the first midnight (the day on which the two transition consents fall due): S6-11, S6-13, CS-07
stages.3: after the second midnight (the following day), or the same day when the tool is told so: CS-08 to CS-13, then the ledger export, the receipts, the verification tool, the test suite and the summary
stages.local chain: the three stages run in one go: the tool moves the time of the chain with evm_increaseTime (300 seconds for the expiry run, then to five minutes after the next midnight, then one day more). It makes that call only when the chain is not Sepolia

KEXP.note: the short window of the expiry run, just under five minutes

KTR.created_by: S6-11 (its first step runs in stage 1)
KTR.birth_date: the date of the trusted time plus one day, minus 18 years
KTR.note: its re-issue after the take-over is KTR2

screens.CREATE: Patient screen, header 'Create Smart Consent Contract': select 'Patient DID (Identity Pointer)', fill 'Authorised Clinician DID', select 'Consent Context (jurisdiction code)', choose 'Data Access Scope (EMR Modules)', fill 'Patient Date of Birth (YYYY-MM-DD, optional)' and 'Conditional Trigger Event (optional)' when the consent has them, fill 'Designated Guardian DIDs (Comma Separated)', set 'Approval Threshold N (guardians who must approve)', fill 'Start Time (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS)' and 'Expiry Time (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS)', click 'Initial Consent', read the consent identifier from the badge
screens.APPROVE: Guardian screen, header 'Guardian Cryptographic Approval': fill 'Enter Target Consent ID', select 'Select Your Guardian DID Identity', click 'Sign Consent via VC'
screens.WAIT_ANCHOR: wait until the ledger holds the ONCHAIN_MINT row SUCCESS of the consent, then open the Guardian screen again for the consent: 'Already anchored on <network> - token #<n>'
screens.REQUEST: Clinician screen, header 'Secure Patient Data Access': fill 'Enter Authorised Consent ID' and 'Your Clinician DID (requester)', select 'Request Context (jurisdiction code)' and 'Purpose of this request', choose 'Select Request Scope', click the button whose label starts with 'Request Data Access', wait for 'Access Granted' or 'Access Denied'
screens.ATTEST: Clinician screen, in 'Conditional triggers waiting for an attestation (1)': click 'Attest this event as <clinician DID>'
screens.PATIENT_REVOKE: Patient screen, 'My Consents': in the row of the consent click 'Revoke'
screens.GUARDIAN_REVOKE: Guardian screen: fill 'Enter Target Consent ID', select 'Select Your Guardian DID Identity', click 'Revoke Consent (as guardian)'
screens.TAKE_OVER: Patient screen, 'My Consents': click 'Take over this consent (age of majority)'
screens.AUDIT: Auditor screen, header 'Blockchain Audit & Consent Lifecycle': select the consent in 'Select Consent to Audit'

about.evidence_names: screens/<file>.png are screenshots. ledger: <ACTION> names the rows that the scenario must find in the audit ledger of the run. receipt: <what> names a transaction whose receipt goes to chain/receipts. service/<id>.json and chain/calls.json hold the answers of the service calls and of the contract calls. test: <file>::<name> names an automated test whose result is taken from tests/junit.xml.
about.test_names_note: Three tests of tests/test_adversarial.py carry a number one higher than their scenario and keep their names: test_A12_non_owner_cannot_mint_or_revoke is the test of A11, test_A13_invalid_or_forged_credential_is_rejected is the test of A12, and test_A11_rewritten_event_changes_its_digest belongs to A13, which is not in this list. The tests of ConsentSBTv4 and of Algorithm 5.1 carry the scenario numbers (test_A11_..., test_A12_... in tests/test_contract_v4.py and tests/test_identity_v2.py).

scenarios.what: A1: an approval signed by a party outside G does not count towards the threshold.

evidence: chain/calls.json (entry S5-08: block, from, function, reason)

one token on the contract (K22, S5-01)
scenarios.can_run_against: Runs against the deployed ConsentSBTv4 as a call (eth_call) from an address that is not the owner. A call returns the refusal of the contract and sends nothing, so there is no receipt and no failed transaction on chain: the evidence is the reason returned by the node and the unchanged state read afterwards. A refused transaction would need a second funded key, which the run does not use. On the local chain the calling address is given test ether first, because that chain refuses a call from an empty address before it reaches the contract. The same three refusals run as transactions in the automated tests on the in-memory chain.

scenarios.expected: The call is refused with the reason 'Ownable: caller is not the owner'. checkValid of the token is still true.

scenarios.what: A11: a transfer of the token is refused by the deployed contract, also for its holder.

K22 issued (S5-01)
scenarios.can_run_against: Runs against the deployed ConsentSBTv4 as a call (eth_call) from an address that is not the owner. A call returns the refusal of the contract and sends nothing, so there is no receipt and no failed transaction on chain: the evidence is the reason returned by the node and the unchanged state read afterwards. A refused transaction would need a second funded key, which the run does not use. On the local chain the calling address is given test ether first, because that chain refuses a call from an empty address before it reaches the contract. The same three refusals run as transactions in the automated tests on the in-memory chain. For the transfer, the holder is the per-consent address, for which nobody holds a key, so a transaction from the holder cannot exist at all: the call is the only form this attack has.

scenarios.what: A12: an invalid or forged credential is refused at creation, at the approval and at the request.
steps: browser, Patient screen: 'Initial Consent' with 'Authorised Clinician DID' did:hospital:999, which holds no credential. Screenshot S5-11_01_patient_clinician_without_credential.png
issuer step, in the process of the tool: credential_status.revoke_credential('did:parent:D') publishes the next status list (the file beside the database of the run)
browser: APPROVE KPEND as did:parent:D. Screenshot S5-11_02_guardian_D_revoked_credential_refused.png
browser: REQUEST on K22 with requester did:parent:A, who holds a guardian credential and no clinician credential, scope Observation. Screenshot S5-11_03_clinician_wrong_role_denied.png

service call: verify_identity('did:hospital:001', role='doctor', credential=<forged>) for five forged credentials: signed by a key that is not the issuer's, from an issuer that is not trusted, with a changed role claim, issued to another identifier, and expired
scenarios.expected: Creation refused: 'The authorised clinician must be one valid DID that holds a valid clinician credential.' The approval of did:parent:D refused and recorded: SIGN_CONSENT REJECTED with the reason CREDENTIAL_REVOKED, the record of KPEND unchanged. The request DENIED with VI failed and no deny code. Each forged credential INVALID.
evidence: ledger: SIGN_CONSENT REJECTED (KPEND, reason CREDENTIAL_REVOKED, credential_checks with Status_valid false), STATE_CHECK and DATA_ACCESS DENIED (K22, requester did:parent:A, failed_checks VI, deny_code null)
needs: KPEND at 1 of 2 (S5-04)
K22 issued (S5-01)
K35 created before this scenario, because its creation verifies the credential of did:parent:D (S5-03)
scenarios.can_run_against: Three forms run against the running application in the browser: a clinician without a credential at creation, a guardian whose credential the issuer has revoked at the approval, and a requester with the wrong role at the request. A forged credential cannot be put before the running application, because its credential store is a file of the repository that the tool does not change: the five forged credentials are given to Algorithm 5.1 by service call and in the automated tests. The revocation of the credential of did:parent:D is final for the database folder of the run.

scenarios.what: The expiry run: a consent with a window of just under five minutes is refused once the window has passed, and the state code is reported, because VT and VL fail together.

scenarios.expected: DENIED with EXPIRED. Failed checks VT and VL, state EXPIRED. By the precedence rule the code is EXPIRED and not POST-VALIDITY.
evidence: ledger: STATE_CHECK (result EXPIRED), DATA_ACCESS DENIED (deny_code EXPIRED, failed_checks VT and VL, time_source block-timestamp, decision_time after the expiry)
test: tests/test_core_v2.py (lines 214 to 228, the precedence rule)
needs: on-chain mode: RPC_URL, PRIVATE_KEY, CONTRACT_V4_ADDRESS, VERIFIER_ADDRESS, and the preflight passed

scenarios.what: The window has passed for a consent that was never issued: the window code POST-VALIDITY is reached.
steps: CREATE KPOST (the same short window as KEXP), APPROVE as did:parent:A only (1/2). Screenshot S6-09_01_guardian_A_1of2.png

scenarios.expected: DENIED with POST-VALIDITY. Failed checks VA, VT and VL, state PENDING_SIGNATURE: the state has no code of its own, so the window code is reported.
evidence: ledger: STATE_CHECK (result PENDING_SIGNATURE), DATA_ACCESS DENIED (deny_code POST-VALIDITY, failed_checks VA, VT, VL)

scenarios.note: An issued consent after its expiry reports EXPIRED, never POST-VALIDITY, because the state code is reported when the state has one. This entry reaches POST-VALIDITY, the ninth code, with a second consent of the same window that was never issued.

The proof is made in the process of the tool with the prover of the same build and is put to the deployed verifier contract as a call (eth_call), which returns the contract's refusal and sends nothing, so no refused proof is left on chain. The same refusals run in the automated tests on the in-memory chain. The other stale root, a consent-tree root that is no longer among the current one and the last eight, would need nine further mints with no revocation between the proof and its presentation: it runs in the automated tests only.
scenarios.note: The contract checks the time before the roots. The kept proof must be presented within 300 seconds of its time t, so the tool builds it immediately before the guardian's Revoke click of S6-02 and presents it immediately after the revoke is confirmed. If the confirmation takes longer than that, the observed reason is 'time is too old' and the scenario is reported FAIL with that reason: it can be run again alone, against the next revocation of the run.
